metadata.title: BDA: letter to all marketing authorisation holders on electronic ICSR reporting in the transitional period
metadata.edition: No date printed (21 July 2012 is a placeholder); applied until 6 months after EudraVigilance functionality was declared · serious ADRs from Bulgaria to the BDA and EudraVigilance within 15 days (English)
metadata.applicability: Marketing authorisation holders (see the PV Info BDA-BG national addendum).

metadata_verification: Source-register metadata; dates and legal status require human verification.
limitations: English rule-based extraction; no GPT or paid API.
Candidates are not approved requirements. Read the original, qualifications and exceptions.
Scans, tables, other languages and implicit obligations may be missed. Zero candidates does not establish zero requirements.

candidates.statement:  All serious ADRs from the territory of Bulgaria should be reported in E2B format within 15 days simultaneously to the BDA (ID-BDA) and to the EudraVigilance, Postauthorisation module (ID-EVHUMAN) .
candidates.context: To all Marketing Authorisation Holder s (MAHs): In accordance with the entry into force of the new European legislation regarding pharmacovigilance of medicinal products for human use, notably Regulation (EC) 726/2004 as amended by Reg ulation (EU) 1235/201 0 and Dir ective 2001/83/EC as amended by Dir ective 2010/84/EU , transposed as required in national legislation regulating medicinal products the Bulgarian Drug Agency (BDA) would like to notify Marketing Authorisation Holders (MAHs) for all medicinal produc ts authorised/registered in Bulgaria, on the following temporary * requirements for ICSRs reporting .  All serious ADRs outside the territory of the European Economic Area (EEA) should be reported in E2B within 15 days to the EudraVigilance, Postauthorisation module (ID-EVHUMAN) only.

candidates.statement:  All serious ADRs outside the territory of the European Economic Area (EEA) should be reported in E2B within 15 days to the EudraVigilance, Postauthorisation module (ID-EVHUMAN) only.
candidates.context:  All serious ADRs from the territory of Bulgaria should be reported in E2B format within 15 days simultaneously to the BDA (ID-BDA) and to the EudraVigilance, Postauthorisation module (ID-EVHUMAN) .  For all non serious ADRs from the territory of Bulgaria, other EEA or non EEA countries – reporting is still not required either to BDA, or to the EudraVigilance.

candidates.statement:  Sponsors of clinical trials should submit electronically SUSARs occurring in Bulgaria to both the EudraVigilance Clinical Trial Module with the messag e receiver identifier EVCTMPROD and to the BDA with the message receiver identifier CTBDAP .
candidates.context: REPORTING RULES The following reporting rules apply to all clinical trials ongoing in Bulgaria:  Sponsors of clinical trial conducted in Bulgaria should report SUSARs occurring outside Bulgaria directly to the EudraVigilance Clinical Trial Module with the messa ge receiver identifier EVCTMPROD . The BDA does not wish to receive SUSARs of foreign origin even if the same study is conducted in Bulgaria and/or if a study with the same investigational medicinal product is conducted in Bulgaria. candidates.statement: For detailed reporting procedures, sponsors should follow the Detailed guidance on the collection, verification and presentation of adverse event/reaction reports arising from clinical trials on medicinal products for human use (‘CT-3’) (Eudravigilance – Clinical Trial Module), (2011/C 172/01).
candidates.context:  all other suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions other than those resulted in death or proven to be life - threatening that have occurred in the course of the clinical trial, 15 days at the latest from receiving the information about their occurrence. The BDA does not require sponsors who are already in production with the EudraVigilance Clinical Trial Module to perform additional tests for the electronic transmission of SUSARs to the message receiver identifier CTBDAP .
